ingestion_rules: Preserve original-language text and edition identity where legally permitted; translations are separate editions.
Keep primary sources separate from modern scholarship and later recollections.
Never infer private thoughts. Attribute motives only when supported by letters, notebooks, diaries or reliable contemporary records.
Represent uncertainty, disagreement, translation ambiguity and missing evidence explicitly.
Use page, section, paragraph or stable fragment citations for every extracted claim.
Do not train or fine-tune on restricted content; store only permitted metadata and links.
Do not treat Google search ranking, OCR output or a single source as truth.
Every generated summary and cross-disciplinary hypothesis retains a source lineage and model/version provenance.
Human review is required before promoting a novel claim to established knowledge.
Speculative disciplines remain labeled speculative until they have formal objects, methods, testable questions and an independent research community.

merlin_integration.canonical_owner: Expert Robot research engine and evidence ledger

logic_lens_case_rules: Scope every case to a named tradition or school, community/context, region, language and date range; never generalize one case to an entire culture.
Every source has edition/version, language, item-level rights status, exact locator and provenance.
Every historical claim and interpretation references one or more known source IDs.
Keep primary sources, translations and secondary scholarship as separate source records.
A formal reconstruction states its logic-system ID, version, syntax, semantics, inference rules, assumptions, preservation claims and limitations.
Every translation records what is preserved and what is lost or changed; equivalence is never assumed from a gloss.
Specialist-reviewed status requires recorded review status and reviewer expertise.
Historical actors' private thoughts and motives are not inferred without traceable evidence.
Formal validity, historical interpretation and cultural context are distinct claim types and are reviewed separately.
